documents.text: To open an account, an applicant must provide a government-issued photo ID and proof of address dated within the last 90 days. Acceptable proof of address includes a utility bill, bank statement, or government letter. A government-issued photo ID may be a passport, driving licence, or national identity card. Applications with missing documents are placed on hold until the documents are received and verified.
documents.title: KYC Documents Required for Account Opening

documents.text: Identity verification checks that the name and date of birth on the government-issued photo ID match the application, that the ID is not expired, and that the applicant's address matches the proof of address. If any field does not match, the case is sent for manual review. Verification must be completed before an account is activated.
documents.title: KYC Identity Verification Steps

documents.text: The onboarding checklist covers identity verification, address verification, risk assessment, and account setup. Onboarding is complete only when identity verification, address verification, and risk assessment are all marked complete. The account setup step creates the account and issues online banking access after the earlier steps pass.
documents.title: Customer Onboarding Checklist

documents.text: AML transaction monitoring reviews transactions for unusual patterns, including large cash deposits, rapid movement of funds, and transactions with high-risk jurisdictions. Suspicious activity is reported to the compliance team for review. Transaction monitoring runs daily and flags cases that exceed the bank's risk thresholds.
documents.title: AML Transaction Monitoring

documents.text: Every applicant is screened against sanctions lists before account opening. A sanctions-list name match blocks autonomous approval and the case is escalated to the compliance team for manual review. No account is opened while a sanctions match is unresolved.
documents.title: Sanctions Screening

documents.text: A politically exposed person is an individual entrusted with a prominent public function. PEP cases receive enhanced due diligence, including a review of the source of funds and senior approval before account opening. PEP status alone does not mean an application is declined, but it does require enhanced due diligence.
documents.title: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) Policy

documents.text: To be eligible to open an account, an applicant must be at least 18 years old, provide valid identity documents, and pass sanctions screening. Applicants who fail sanctions screening are not eligible for autonomous approval. Eligibility is confirmed only after identity verification and risk assessment are complete.
documents.title: Account Opening Eligibility

documents.text: Transactions and applicants connected to high-risk jurisdictions receive enhanced due diligence and additional monitoring. High-risk jurisdiction cases are reviewed by the compliance team and may require extra documentation about the source of funds before approval.
documents.title: High-Risk Jurisdictions

documents.text: Suspected fraud should be reported to the fraud team immediately, and the affected account may be temporarily restricted while the report is investigated. Customers should not share passwords or one-time codes with anyone claiming to be from the bank. Fraud reports are reviewed within one business day.
documents.title: Reporting Suspected Fraud

documents.text: To change the address on an account, a customer must provide proof of the new address dated within the last 90 days and verify their identity. Address changes take effect after identity verification is complete. A utility bill or bank statement can serve as proof of the new address.
documents.title: Changing Your Address on an Account

documents.text: Online banking access is issued after onboarding is complete and identity verification has passed. Customers sign in with a username and password and confirm sign-in with a one-time code. If access is locked, identity verification is required before access is restored.
documents.title: Online Banking Access

documents.text: For large deposits, the bank may request documentation about the source of funds, such as a payslip, sale agreement, or business invoice. Source of funds documentation is reviewed by the compliance team before large deposits are accepted. Failure to provide it can delay account activation.
documents.title: Source of Funds Documentation
